newsitem.title: USA: Six die as two small planes collide over Chicago.
newsitem.headline: Six die as two small planes collide over Chicago.

text.p: Two small planes collided Saturday and rained burning wreckage into Lake Michigan in front of horrified bathers, authorities said.
Authorities recovered the bodies of four women and two men from the wreckage of the two planes. Names of the dead were not released.
A Beech Bonanza on approach to Meigs Field, a small airport along Chicago's downtown lakefront, collided with the other small plane about six miles south of the airfield.

The pilot of the Bonanza was in communication with controllers and was preparing to land, a spokesman for the Federal Aviation Administration said. "The preliminary report was that the other aircraft was transiting the airspace," spokesman Don Zochert said.

The planes collided about 60 yards offshore, shearing off the wing of the unidentified plane, which burst into flames and plunged into the lake within sight of the busy lakefront near the popular Museum of Science and Industry.
The Bonanza continued on for less than a mile before it went down.
